chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Muhrim (person in Ihram) who enters the bathhouse. He said, 'He does not enter.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram, a ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram entering a bathhouse?
ai.summary: This concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the prohibition of a Muhrim entering the hammam, reflecting the broader principle of maintaining ritual purity and avoiding actions that might lead to the loss of Ihram status. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often contextualized within the conditions of the body and clothing, where excessive heat or sweating in the bathhouse could potentially invalidate the state of consecration or require specific expiations if boundaries are crossed.
